sectionTitle: Cosmic Origin, Causation, and Temporal Boundaries

lockedMove.speaker: William Lane Craig
lockedMove.excerpt: that I've addressed this question recently on my website uh reasonablefaith.org every week I take a different question from readers and about two or three weeks ago I took the question about whether or not causation requires the existence of time and I don't see any good reason to think that uh causation does require the existence of time think of it this way cause and effect can surely be simultanous think of a heavy chandelier hanging from a chain from the ceiling clearly it is the ceiling that is supporting the chandelier it's not the chandelier that is pushing up the ceiling the the causal
lockedMove.proposition: Causation need not precede its effect; creation can be simultaneous with the universe’s first moment as God becomes temporal.
